references.text: The Lord speaks with Moses face to face, mouth to mouth, and not in riddles - the same close communication described in Exodus 33:11
Confirms that no prophet has arisen in Israel whom the Lord knew face to face, as with Moses
Jacob names the place Peniel because he saw God face to face - the same expression 'פָּנִים אֶל־פָּנִים' is used
The Lord spoke with the people face to face on the mountain, out of the fire
Joshua is mentioned as Moses' servant, the same role described in Exodus 33:11
Joshua, son of Nun, is described as Moses' servant from his youth, corresponding to the description 'נַעַר' (young man/servant)
Joshua is introduced as the son of Nun and Moses' servant, the same identification as in Exodus 33:11
The first time Joshua is mentioned in the Bible, already then in Moses' service
No one has ever seen God, but the only Son has made him known - stands in contrast to Moses' experience of speaking with God face to face
We who with unveiled faces behold the Lord's glory - alludes to Moses' face-to-face meeting with God
Illuminates the intimate 'face-to-face' communication by linking it to the practice of the veil.
Plays on the transition from Joshua as a young assistant to the Spirit-filled leader after Moses' death.
Connects Joshua's presence at the tent to his full obedience in carrying out God's commands through Moses.
Links Joshua's early role as a young man at the tent to his formal commissioning with God's Spirit.
